input: intervals is a plain dense Array of plain dense two-element Arrays [start, end]; each endpoint is a Number integer. Every interval represents a half-open meeting [start, end) with start < end. The calendar may be empty, unsorted, contain duplicate meetings or share row objects. Zero-length and reversed meetings are outside the domain. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: A nonnegative Number integer, at most n, giving the minimum rooms needed for all meetings, equal to peak simultaneous occupancy. Empty input returns 0. A meeting ending at time t does not overlap one starting at t. The sweep releases every end <= the next start before allocating that start; positive meeting durations ensure no unstarted meeting is released.
mutation_aliasing: No writes to the supplied outer list/array or any interval row. Only new endpoint arrays are sorted. Shared input rows remain shared and unchanged. The result is a scalar; no retained references or persistent Solution instance state.
numeric: Endpoints are safe integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]; NaN, infinities, BigInt, sparse arrays, proxies and accessor properties are excluded. Array lengths, indices and room counters up to n <= 4294967295 are exact Numbers. The sorting comparator uses relational comparisons, not endpoint subtraction. No arithmetic is performed on endpoint values, and signed-zero identity is not distinguished.
complexity: n is the number of meetings. O(n log(n + 1)) time for two endpoint sorts plus O(n) scanning; O(n) auxiliary space for both endpoint copies and sorting workspace, assuming an Array.sort implementation with O(n log(n + 1)) comparisons and O(n) workspace. ECMAScript does not guarantee sort time or space bounds; the eventual qualified runtime must establish these assumptions. Each start and each consumed end is processed once, so the nested release loop is linear in total; no heap is used.

helpers.name: sortedEndpoints
helpers.contract: Returns two fresh Arrays of numeric endpoint values: starts sorted ascending and ends independently sorted ascending. Original interval order and rows are unchanged; sorting does not retain meeting pair correspondence.
helpers.cost: One call per candidate. Two O(n) endpoint copies and two comparison sorts, O(n log(n + 1)) time and O(n) auxiliary space including sort workspace under the declared runtime assumptions. Its complete identical definition is included in both meeting candidates. The helper definition is 403 UTF-8 bytes including its terminal newline.

helpers.name: compareEndpoints
helpers.contract: Nested comparator returns -1, 0 or 1 by numeric order, without subtracting endpoints.
helpers.cost: O(1) per comparison on safe Number integers; complete source is included inside sortedEndpoints and charged for both candidates.

source_accounting: Standalone UTF-8 source is 915 bytes. All endpoint-copy construction, comparator source where present, sort invocations, helper definitions, Solution class, method, loops and result logic are charged as standalone source. The shared helper is fully included in each file, not imported. Any eventual judge adapter must also be charged.
evidence_boundary: Independently authored dev_fit candidate outside frozen source sets. No candidate execution, predecessor equivalence, behavioral qualification, benchmark acceptance or M1 progress is claimed. Remaining gates: bind the frozen problem contract and judge interface, run independent cases in the approved isolated judge, and retain source-bound receipts and failures. Syntax checks alone do not qualify this candidate.
